What is MagicSchool?

A large library of 80+ purpose-built AI tools for teachers - lesson plans, rubrics, IEP goals, parent emails, differentiated texts - plus a separate safe student-facing environment (MagicStudent) with teacher-monitored rooms.

Best for

Cutting teacher administrative workload with task-specific generators.

Main features

  • 80+ task-specific generators (lesson plan, unit plan, rubric, exit ticket, IEP goal, behaviour intervention, parent email translated into any language)
  • MagicStudent rooms with teacher monitoring and flagged-content alerts
  • Raina AI assistant
  • text leveller and translator
  • LMS integrations
  • district analytics dashboard.

Practical use cases

  • Generating a differentiated lesson plan in minutes
  • writing IEP goals
  • drafting a sensitive parent email and translating it into the family's home language
  • levelling a reading passage for mixed abilities
  • building rubrics.

Who is it for?

  • K-12 teachers, instructional coaches, special-education staff, school and district administrators.

Pricing, free access & limits

Freemium for individual teachers; per-teacher or per-student district licensing

Plans described in the source

Free plan for individual educators covering most tools with monthly generation limits. MagicSchool Plus around $99.96/yr (about $8.33/mo) per teacher for unlimited generations and premium tools. Enterprise/district licensing quoted per teacher or per student, typically with LMS/SIS integration, SSO and admin analytics included.

Free plan

Yes - a genuinely usable free tier for individual teachers covering the bulk of the tool library.

Free trial

Plus trials offered; district pilots arranged through sales.

Usage limits to consider

Free tier caps monthly generations and limits access to some premium tools and MagicStudent room capacity.

Confirm current plans and pricing ↗

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • The task-specific tool design means teachers do not have to learn prompting
  • enormous time savings on administrative writing
  • multilingual parent communication is a standout for diverse districts
  • free tier is genuinely generous
  • strong student-safety monitoring.

Limitations to consider

  • Output is generic without heavy teacher editing
  • quality varies by tool
  • the sheer number of tools is overwhelming at first
  • student data governance needs careful review before district rollout
  • largely US-curriculum oriented.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web
  • Google Classroom, Canvas, Schoology integrations
  • Chrome extension

Languages

  • Output in 30+ languages including Arabic and French - particularly strong for parent communication

API access

Enterprise integrations rather than an open API

Integrations and exports

  • Google Classroom, Canvas, Schoology, Clever, ClassLink, Google Drive, Microsoft Teams for Education

Evaluation notes

Every output needs teacher review before it reaches students - treat it as a first-draft engine. The parent-communication translation is the feature teachers report using most.
